newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - BT brushes off rivals, sees growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - BT brushes off rivals, sees growth.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc said on Thursday that it expected to grow both in its home markets and abroad despite stiff competition from international rivals, cable and mobile telephone companies.
Finance director Robert Brace told Reuters that the group had beaten analysts expectations in the first half and second quarter because of good volume growth.
"We're growing, we're not going backwards," Brace said.
BT's has hung onto its 20.5 million residential customer lines over the last 12 months despite predictions that competition from cable companies would force numbers down.

"The market grows by around two percent per annum and the cable companies have come and taken lines -- but they haven't really generated new business," Brace said. "The amount taken is much less than they hoped for which means that our base is still flat to growing."
BT said its biggest business -- inland calls -- had grown by one percent to over seven percent in the quarter on a 12 month moving average basis after price cuts and marketing initiatives.
